summary: The document is a non-functional placeholder containing seven highly ambiguous, untestable statements for a food delivery mobile app. It lacks all standard software engineering artifacts, including scope, user roles, technical constraints, and acceptance criteria, rendering it completely unusable for development or QA planning.

risk_factors.title: Unspecified Payment Security
risk_factors.description: Requirement 4 states 'Customers can pay somehow,' providing zero guidance on PCI-DSS compliance, tokenization, or supported payment gateways, creating a massive liability and integration risk.
risk_factors.mitigation: Define specific payment providers (e.g., Stripe, PayPal), mandate PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, and specify tokenization strategies for card data.

risk_factors.title: Undefined Data Privacy & PII Handling
risk_factors.description: The app involves customer addresses, phone numbers, and order history, but there are no GDPR/CCPA requirements, data retention policies, or encryption standards specified.
risk_factors.mitigation: Add a Data Privacy section detailing PII classification, encryption at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.3), and user data deletion workflows.

risk_factors.title: Unmeasurable Performance SLAs
risk_factors.description: Requirement 3 'Delivery should happen fast' is subjective. Without defined latency targets for API responses or delivery time windows, the backend architecture cannot be properly sized.
risk_factors.mitigation: Define specific SLAs, e.g., 'API response time < 200ms for 95% of requests' and 'Delivery ETA accuracy within +/- 5 minutes'.

risk_factors.title: Lack of Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
risk_factors.description: Requirement 5 'Restaurants should manage things' does not define user roles (Admin, Restaurant Owner, Driver, Customer), leading to potential privilege escalation vulnerabilities.
risk_factors.mitigation: Define a strict RBAC matrix specifying permissions for each user role, including data visibility and action capabilities.

conflicts_and_ambiguities.suggested_resolution: Replace with measurable UX metrics, such as 'Task completion rate > 90%' or 'App Store rating target > 4.5 stars'.
Specify the maximum number of taps from app launch to order confirmation (e.g., 'Max 5 taps to place an order').
List supported payment methods (Credit Card, Apple Pay, Cash on Delivery) and specify the primary payment gateway integration.
Enumerate specific management functions: menu editing, order status updates, daily sales reporting, and staff management.

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: Without a defined scope, the project will suffer from scope creep, and stakeholders will have misaligned expectations regarding MVP features.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Add a section defining the MVP scope, out-of-scope features, and primary business objectives (e.g., 'Launch in 3 cities with 50 restaurants').

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: The system cannot be designed without knowing who the users are. Different roles require different UI flows and backend permissions.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Define personas for Customer, Restaurant Owner, Delivery Driver, and System Admin, including their primary goals and pain points.

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: The current statements are not functional requirements. Developers need specific, testable behaviors to implement.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Break down features into user stories with acceptance criteria, e.g., 'As a customer, I want to filter restaurants by cuisine type so that I can find food I like.'

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: Performance, security, and scalability are critical for a delivery app but are entirely absent.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Specify NFRs including: Availability (99.9%), Scalability (handle 10,000 concurrent users), Security (OWASP Top 10 compliance), and Compatibility (iOS 15+, Android 10+).

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: No mention of how data will be stored or how the app will integrate with third-party services (maps, payments, SMS).
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Define the core data entities (User, Restaurant, Order, Delivery) and list required third-party APIs (e.g., Google Maps, Twilio, Stripe).

ai_recommendations: Completely discard the current document and initiate a formal requirements elicitation workshop with stakeholders to define the MVP scope and user personas.
Adopt a structured requirements framework (e.g., User Stories with Acceptance Criteria) to replace the current ambiguous statements, ensuring every requirement is testable and measurable.

Engage a security architect to define the initial security and data privacy requirements, specifically focusing on PCI-DSS compliance for payments and GDPR/CCPA for customer PII, before any development begins.
